subjective: The pet parent reports that Miko was unvaccinated at the time of a previous trial. Deworming was last done in November. Miko is currently pregnant. The pet parent is concerned about safe deworming during pregnancy and the presence of skin lesions on the face with some bleeding. Miko tends to roam and may get scared, especially in rain. There was a recent incident where Miko got scared due to a bump after her last dinner. The pet parent inquires about the age at which kittens can be separated and expresses concern about the pregnancy status and health of the kittens. There is also mention of some redness and possible injury from a fight and slight greenish eye discharge.
objective: Physical examination revealed facial skin lesions under the skin resembling a scab or mask, with one fresh lesion noted. There is some redness on certain areas, possibly from injury. Eye discharge is present but considered normal. No other abnormalities were noted. Ultrasonography is recommended to assess fetal heart function and pregnancy status as physical examination alone is insufficient.
assessment: Miko is a pregnant female cat with facial skin lesions, some bleeding, and mild redness possibly due to injury. The pregnancy status and fetal health require ultrasonographic evaluation. The skin lesions may be due to fungal or bacterial infection, but antifungal treatments are limited due to pregnancy. The eye discharge is mild and not currently concerning. There is a risk of vomiting with deworming medication, but no expected harm to the fetuses.
plan:
Diagnostic: Perform ultrasonography to assess fetal heart function and estimate delivery date.
Therapeutic: Administer a pregnancy-safe deworming tablet mixed with wet food. Provide a topical spray and ointment safe for use during pregnancy to apply on the affected skin areas, avoiding the nose and other sensitive areas. Avoid coconut oil unless the wound is dry and scarred.
Preventive: Monitor for signs of worsening skin lesions or infection.
Monitoring: Observe for any vomiting or adverse reactions to medication. Monitor eye discharge and skin lesion healing.
Owner Instructions: Apply medications as directed, avoid applying ointment on the nose, monitor Miko's behavior and wound condition, and consider ultrasonography for pregnancy evaluation. Separation of kittens should be done after 2 months, ideally after 6 months. Taking Miko to the clinic is optional based on owner preference.
conclusion: Miko is a pregnant domestic cat presenting with facial skin lesions and mild redness likely due to injury or infection. Deworming is planned with a pregnancy-safe tablet formulation. Ultrasonography is recommended to evaluate fetal health and pregnancy status as physical examination is insufficient. Topical treatments will be applied to the skin lesions with precautions to avoid sensitive areas. Eye discharge is mild and not currently concerning. The owner is advised on medication administration, monitoring for side effects, and timing for kitten separation. Follow-up ultrasonography and monitoring of skin lesions are advised.
